P1.evidence: No setter on this call. Three-part frame only — 'I just want to get a good idea where you're at, you know, really build out what it is that you want. And then if there's alignment, we can talk about the coaching' — 'what's in the way' omitted. Agreement asked for and given ('Alrighty?' / 'Okay'), then the open question: 'What were you hoping we could potentially help you out with?'

P2.evidence: The single most consequential miss in the batch: a cardiac condition and fifteen years of daily 25 mg prednisone arrived entirely unprompted at 00:13:46, because the rep never asked a health-conditions question. Age (68 in July), height, weight, waist and business ownership were all volunteered. He did follow up the fracture once — 'Are you still in a boot now?' — and did probe results properly ('How long did it take you to lose it?', 'How long have you kind of been at 294?'). Sleep and energy never came up.

P3.evidence: Good surface work — 'if we were to fast forward six months down the line, what's really the goal for you?' and 'What else would change at that point when you get to 160?' — which surfaced floor work, clothing and overall comfort. Then it stopped. He never asked what is driving this now, never asked who else it impacts, and never reflected it back, despite the prospect having just become a grandfather ('our daughter just had a baby') and having said the thing that mattered most: 'it's embarrassing when I get on the floor and somebody wants to help me get up.' None of that was developed.

P4.evidence: Asked the why-didn't-it-stick question well — 'You've kind of gone off plan a little bit or not sticking to it as much as you were. What, why do you feel like that is?' — and the prospect named the gap himself: laziness, running the business, no meal prep, and the fracture as the trigger point. Prior attempts were never explored and the 'why can't you stick to it on your own' question was never asked.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame at all, on the call in this batch that had the most raw material for one — 68 years old, plateaued four months, a heart condition, and a man who cannot get off the floor unassisted. Nothing was asked about what the next two years look like if nothing changes, and no line was drawn in the sand. This left the spouse conversation with no urgency behind it.

P6.evidence: A readiness question was asked before presenting — 'do you feel like you're ready to punch laziness in the face and really go for it?' — answered with a soft 'I feel like I am', and the rep moved to presentation anyway. The belief question was eventually asked, but after the price as part of the spouse objection: 'speaking to Selly aside, do you feel like we can actually help you get to where you want to be?' The 'any reason you wouldn't go all in' question never ran.

P11.evidence: Close attempted — both tiers priced, guarantee delivered, tier preference obtained ('I've been looking more at the six months') and same-day onboarding described: 'we would obviously get you onboarded on this call... process the investment and get you all onboarded today.' But payment was never actually asked for; the rep went to 'Any questions or how do you feel about it?' and took the spouse deferral. Once payment was deferred, the onboarding call, agreement and welcome-email steps were unreachable.

objection_plays.detail: The best-run play in the batch so far. He asked her name to personalise it, isolated correctly — 'the most important part, speaking to Selly aside, do you feel like we can actually help you get to where you want to be?' — pressure-tested the yes with 'You sure?', pre-framed the two ways the conversation goes, asked 'How do you feel like she's going to feel about it?' and 'if she did say no, what would you do?', then time-boxed it and booked a specific follow-up. What did not run: 'is there any reason she would NOT want you stronger and less in pain', the 'is this needing her input or asking permission to bet on yourself' challenge, the 'this isn't a joint decision like buying a house' frame, and the deposit-with-refund fallback.

Money was in the room twice — 'it'll be 6,000' as the stated reason for needing his wife, and two simultaneous house purchases named as why she would hesitate. No OC move ran at all: no finances-aside isolation, no SHOULD-I versus HOW frame, no offer to break the payment up, and no financial picture. Payment plans were never mentioned on this call, which is notable given the rep raised third-party instalments unprompted on another call the same week.

Free alternative already available to him: if his wife says no he plans to ask his Sifu to program for him and take up training partners' offers of help — 'I would talk to Sifu for sure and see if maybe he would put me on something' and 'I've had them, you know, reach out to me and say, hey, you know, if you want, I'll help you.' No scripted play exists for a competent free substitute inside the prospect's own community, and the rep did not address it.

Clinical fit: a heart condition, fifteen years of prednisone and a fracture still in a boot. There is no scripted path for medical suitability, and the rep improvised by underwriting it himself — 'you probably wouldn't be able to do the kettlebell stuff with a boot on. You could, just not the leg stuff' — and then turned it into a selling point. This is the script gap the ICP observations already identify, showing up in its most severe form yet.

notes: Warm, well-paced call with a genuinely good spouse play and a real follow-up booked — and almost no diagnosis under it. Baseline and the consequence frame were skipped entirely, which is how a cardiac history and a live fracture ended up as volunteered asides rather than qualifying facts. The single correction that matters here is not a sales move: a health-conditions question in Phase 2 would have changed what this call should have been.
